I added `ExternalLinkHelper` in `app/helpers/external_link_helper.rb`. Its `external_link_to(text, href)` renders a normal `link_to`, plus `rel="external"` when the href's host is not `Whitehall.public_host`. The three tests I added in `test/unit/app/helpers/external_link_helper_test.rb` pass.

```ruby
module ExternalLinkHelper
  def external_link_to(text, href)
    host = Addressable::URI.parse(href).host

    if host && host != Whitehall.public_host
      link_to(text, href, rel: "external")
    else
      link_to(text, href)
    end
  end
end
```

Relative links have no host, so they get no `rel`. Links to the public host also get none.

- `https://example.com/a` renders with `rel="external"`.

```ruby
module ExternalLinkHelper
  def external_link_to(text, href)
    host = Addressable::URI.parse(href)&.host
    options = host && host != Whitehall.public_host ? { rel: "external" } : {}
    link_to(text, href, options)
  end
end
```

Choices I made:
- **Host check:** It compares against `Whitehall.public_host`, the same host `ApplicationHelper#is_external?` uses. I didn't call `is_external?` directly, so the helper doesn't depend on another helper being mixed in.
- **Relative links:** They get no `rel`, because they have no host and so don't point anywhere else.
